newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian franc to enter EMU at central rate -cen.bank.
newsitem.headline: Belgian franc to enter EMU at central rate -cen.bank.

text.p: The Belgian central bank expects the franc to enter the European Union's single currency at its central rate of 20.6255 to the mark within the EU's exchange rate mechanism.
The expectation implies a strengthening of the franc between now and 1999 when European Union countries are due to begin the third and final phase of economic and monetary union (EMU).

"Looking ahead, there is no reason why the conversion rate of the franc should diverge from its central rate to the German mark at the (1999) start of...EMU," governor Alfons Verplaetse told a news conference on the bank's annual report on Wednesday.
His comments were embargoed for Friday.

When he spoke the franc was at around 20.6300/30 to the mark, having weakened earlier this year following news on a series of corruption scandals involving the French-speaking socialist partner in the ruling centre-left coalition.

Verplaetse said the central bank was not worried by "slight" movements of the franc away from its central rate in the semi-fixed ERM currency grid, but he refused to specify at what point it would intervene. He did not define "slight".
Last week a Belgian paper quoted Verplaetse as saying that the franc's recent weakness was "ridiculous".
In 1996 the central bank bought 300 billion francs worth of foreign currency to avoid an excessive rise in the franc.
Moving on to central bank policy in EMU, Verplaetse said a future European Central Bank (ECB) should set money supply targets rather than inflation targets to create price stability.
"The preference (among EU member states) seems to go towards a money supply policy. We too are in favour of this," he said.
At present the Belgian central bank, like many others in the European Union, follows the Bundesbank's lead. The German central bank already uses money supply targeting and with noted success.
A minority, including Britain, use inflation targeting.
Final decisions on policy will be taken once the ECB is set up in 1998. It will take over responsibility for interest rate policy once the single currency is launched in 1999.
On the Belgian economy, Verplaetse said he expected Gross Domestic Product to grow by at least two percent in 1997 from 1.4 percent in 1996.
In its autumn 1996 forecasts the European Union saw 1997 GDP growing at 2.2 percent.
Verplaetse said the Belgian central bank, which has been a major seller of gold in recent years, planned no further sales.
"When I became governor (in 1990) we had 1,300 tonnes of gold. Now we have 600 tonnes. We did enough. I can live with our current level of gold assets," he said.
"Given the current gold price on the market...I think many other countries are unhappy that they have not done what we did," he added.
Belgium's most recent gold sale was in March when the bank sold 203 tonnes to an unspecified central bank. Gold was then quoted at around $400 an ounce. It was at $345 on Wednesday.
